AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA VI
Dr. Aron Vale

Model run 889 complete. Result unchanged. Large-scale incineration increases long-range dispersal. Firestorm conditions increase it substantially. High-energy explosive demolition produces similar effects.
Nuclear thermal columns are worse. I've rewritten the conclusion so many times it no longer sounds like language. Maybe the graffiti version is better. STOP BURNING IT.

Fire kills colonies. Yes. It also creates transport. Both statements can be true. We are trapped because the first effect is visible immediately and the second arrives hundreds of kilometers away days later.
Human beings are catastrophically vulnerable to anything that rewards us now and punishes us later.

AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA VII
Atmospheric Technician
Continuity transmission acknowledged by Strategic Command. So they heard us. Important distinction. People later may say they never knew. They knew.

They had Vale's model. They had the sampling. They had uncertainty ranges. They also had four cities reporting uncontrolled growth, a collapsing refugee corridor, and a government demanding visible action.
Command response: operational necessity outweighs projected dispersal risk.
I don't know whether that was wrong. I know what happened afterward. Sometimes knowing isn't the same thing as having a choice.
